mainTopic: A טמא eating קדשים before זריקה, טמא meat and wood and frankincense, and whether offering a non-kosher or wild animal on the מזבח violates a command
overview: The גמרא finishes ריש לקיש's היקש: just as a טמא entering the מקדש gets כרת, 'בכל קדש לא תגע' must refer to eating קדשים, not touching them. It then asks how ריש לקיש can use this פסוק, since he already needs it to give מלקות to a טמא who ate before זריקה. The answer is that the extra word 'כל' teaches both laws. אביי and רבא then agree that the dispute about eating before זריקה concerns a טמא person, but they differ about טמא meat. אביי says all agree there are מלקות, because 'והבשר' includes even wood and frankincense. רבא says all agree there are none, and he explains that wood and frankincense count only once sanctified in a כלי, as a משנה teaches. Next comes a new מחלוקת about offering a בהמה טמאה on the מזבח, which turns on whether a לאו הבא מכלל עשה carries מלקות. After רבי ירמיה's challenge, רבי יעקב moves the dispute to offering a חיה. רבא then challenges ריש לקיש with a ברייתא that uses the parable of a student told to bring 'only wheat'. That ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the comparison between holy food and the Temple
steps.stepSummary: Just as entering the מקדש while טמא carries כרת, the prohibition about קדש must also carry כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Just as the Temple is something whose violation carries] the taking of a life, so too the holy item is something whose violation carries the taking of a life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a comparison it started just before this: the פסוק puts 'קדש' next to 'מקדש', so the two are compared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא who enters the מקדש gets כרת, which the גמרא calls 'taking of a life'. Because the פסוק links the two, the prohibition about קדש must also be one that carries כרת. This sets up the next step, which asks what kind of act that could be.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking of a life; here it means the punishment of כָּרֵת
Holy items, meaning sacrificial food
A comparison learned from two things placed side by side in a פסוק

phrases.english: the taking of a life,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence that began just before: just as entering the מקדש while טמא carries כרת.

phrases.aramaic: אַף קוֹדֶשׁ – דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ נְטִילַת נְשָׁמָה.
phrases.english: so too, the holy item is a matter that carries the taking of a life.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף קוֹדֶשׁ – דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ נְטִילַת נְשָׁמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the היקש begun on the previous daf
steps.raayaObject: That the קדש prohibition in 'בכל קדש לא תגע' carries כרת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The היקש to 'ואל המקדש לא תבא' (ויקרא 12:4)

steps.title: It cannot mean touching, so it must mean eating
steps.stepSummary: Touching קדשים never carries כרת, so 'לא תגע' must be talking about eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is about touching, is there any taking of a life for that?! Rather, it is about eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the פסוק's word 'touch' really means eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא who touches קדשים does not get כרת. Since the comparison requires a prohibition that carries כרת, the only possibility is a טמא who eats קדשים. This gives ריש לקיש his warning (אזהרה) for a טמא who eats sacrificial food.

keyTerms.meaning: Touching
Eating
Is there? (a rhetorical 'of course not')

steps.whatToRemember: For ריש לקיש, 'בכל קדש לא תגע' is the warning against a טמא eating קדשים, not touching them.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק says 'touch', but the גמרא proves it is really talking about eating.

phrases.english: And if it is about touching,
is there any taking of a life for that?!
Rather, it is about eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בְּנוֹגֵעַ – נְטִילַת נְשָׁמָה מִי אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the כרת requirement to rule out touching
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'בכל קדש לא תגע' refers to a טמא eating קדשים.

steps.title: Challenge: the verse is needed for eating before the sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש already uses this פסוק for a טמא who ate before זריקה, so how can he also use it here?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he still needs this verse for an impure person who ate holy meat before the sprinkling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: he already uses this פסוק to teach a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק is busy teaching that a טמא who eats before זריקה gets מלקות, it seems it cannot also serve as the general warning for a טמא who eats קדשים. One פסוק normally does not teach two separate laws unless something in it shows that it does.

keyTerms.meaning: But still
He needs it (for another teaching)
Sprinkling of the blood on the מזבח, which makes the meat permitted
A ritually impure person

phrases.english: But still, he needs it
for an impure person who ate holy meat
before the sprinkling!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's use of the פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's use of 'בכל קדש לא תגע' as the warning for a טמא eating
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already used for the case of eating before זריקה, so it seems unavailable for this teaching.

steps.title: The dispute about eating before the sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says a טמא who eats before זריקה gets מלקות; רבי יוחנן says he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: An impure person who ate holy meat before the sprinkling: ריש לקיש said he is flogged, and רבי יוחנן said he is not flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source of the challenge, a known מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before זריקה, the meat is not yet permitted even to a טהור person. The question is whether the special prohibition against a טמא eating still applies at that point. ריש לקיש says it does, and רבי יוחנן says it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: He receives מלקות (lashes)
He does not receive lashes

phrases.english: As it was stated:

phrases.aramaic: טָמֵא שֶׁאָכַל בְּשַׂר קוֹדֶשׁ לִפְנֵי זְרִיקָה –
phrases.english: An impure person who ate holy meat before the sprinkling:
Reish Lakish said: he is flogged,
and Rabbi Yochanan said: he is not flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the challenge
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש: מלקות for a טמא eating before זריקה; רבי יוחנן: no מלקות.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's source: the verse makes no time distinction
steps.stepSummary: 'בכל קדש לא תגע' does not limit itself to a certain time, so it includes before זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said he is flogged because of 'You shall not touch any holy thing': it makes no difference whether it is before the sprinkling or after the sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why ריש לקיש says the person gets מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק forbids a טמא to eat קדש without mentioning any time. So for ריש לקיש it covers both before and after זריקה. This is exactly why the challenge said he 'needs' this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall not touch any holy thing' (ויקרא 12:4)
It makes no difference

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said he is flogged:
'You shall not touch any holy thing,'
it makes no difference whether before the sprinkling
or after the sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of the dispute
steps.raayaObject: מלקות for a טמא eating before זריקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The open-ended wording of 'בכל קדש לא תגע'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's source: the warning applies only after sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns the warning through ברדלא's גזירה שוה of 'טומאתו', and that פסוק is about meat after זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said he is not flogged, as ברדלא taught: it is learned from 'his impurity' and 'his impurity', and when that verse is written, it is about after the sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן says there is no מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the warning against a טמא eating comes from a גזירה שוה with entering the מקדש, not from 'בכל קדש לא תגע'. The פסוק that says 'טומאתו' about eating speaks of meat that is already permitted. So the warning, and therefore מלקות, applies only after זריקה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned (by comparison)
'His impurity', the shared word of the גזירה שוה
A teaching learned from the same word appearing in two places

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said he is not flogged,
as Bardela taught:
it is learned from 'his impurity' and 'his impurity',
phrases.notes: The same word appears for eating קדשים and for entering the מקדש, linking the two laws.

phrases.english: and when that verse is written, it is about after the sprinkling.
phrases.notes: The eating פסוק (ויקרא 7:20) talks about meat that is already permitted, which means after זריקה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second side of the dispute
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברדלא's גזירה שוה of 'טומאתו', with the eating פסוק referring to after זריקה

steps.title: The word 'every' teaches both laws
steps.stepSummary: The extra word 'כל' shows that the פסוק teaches both the basic warning and the case before זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse say 'a holy thing'. Why does it say 'any holy thing'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge for ריש לקיש by pointing to an extra word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק only taught one law, it could have said just 'בקדש'. The extra 'כל' widens it, so ריש לקיש learns both the warning for a טמא eating and the inclusion of eating before זריקה. The challenge from step 3 is resolved.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let the verse say
Learn two things from it

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש uses the word 'כל' in 'בכל קדש' to learn two laws: the warning against a טמא eating קדשים, and that it applies even before זריקה.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say 'a holy thing';
why does it say 'any holy thing'?
Learn two things from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra word in the פסוק teaches a second law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק can teach only one law, so it would be used up by the before-זריקה case
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כל' is extra, so the פסוק teaches both laws

steps.title: Returning to the dispute itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the מחלוקת between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן so it can analyze it further.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself: a טמא person who ate קדשים meat before the blood was sprinkled. ריש לקיש says he gets lashes. רבי יוחנן says he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the word 'גופא' to go back and quote the מחלוקת again. This is a setup line that prepares for the new explanations of אביי and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is decided here. The גמרא brings back the exact dispute from earlier (step 4) because the next lines ask exactly what case it covers.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself': a signal that the גמרא is returning to a statement it quoted earlier in order to discuss it directly
Sprinkling the קרבן's blood on the מזבח, which makes the meat permitted to eat
He gets מלקות (lashes)

phrases.english: The matter itself:

phrases.aramaic: טָמֵא שֶׁאָכַל בְּשַׂר קוֹדֶשׁ לִפְנֵי זְרִיקָה,
phrases.english: An impure person who ate sacrificial meat before the sprinkling of the blood:
Reish Lakish says: he is flogged,
Rabbi Yochanan says: he is not flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the original מחלוקת after the side discussion in steps 5-7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש: a טמא who eats before זריקה gets מלקות; רבי יוחנן: he does not.

steps.title: אביי limits the dispute to an impure person
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the מחלוקת is only about a טמא person; if the meat is טמא, everyone agrees he gets מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They argue when the person's body is טמא. But when the meat is טמא, everyone agrees he gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains exactly which case ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue about. He separates a טמא person from טמא meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two different איסורים: a טמא person eating קדשים, and anyone eating קדשים meat that became טמא. אביי says the argument is only about the first one. For טמא meat eaten before זריקה, both agree there are מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity of the body: the person eating is טמא
Impurity of the meat: the קדשים meat itself became טמא
Everyone agrees

phrases.english: Abaye said: The dispute is about impurity of the body,
but with impurity of the meat,
everyone agrees he is flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact case of the מחלוקת just restated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is only about a טמא person; for טמא meat before זריקה, all agree there are מלקות.

steps.title: אביי's source: even wood and frankincense are included
steps.stepSummary: The extra word 'והבשר' includes wood and frankincense, which are not even food, so meat before זריקה is surely included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says 'and the meat', which comes to include wood and frankincense. They are not things people eat, and even so the פסוק included them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for אביי's view that טמא meat before זריקה brings מלקות. It uses the extra word 'והבשר' in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איסור of eating טמא קדשים was stretched by the פסוק to cover wood and frankincense of the מזבח, which are not normal food at all. If those count, then real meat that just isn't permitted yet (before זריקה) certainly counts too.

keyTerms.meaning: To include: the extra word adds more cases to the rule
Wood (for the מזבח fire) and frankincense
Things fit to be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: The proof works as a קל וחומר: if even non-food is included, edible meat that is only waiting for זריקה is included all the more.

phrases.english: As the verse says: 'And the meat'
to include wood and frankincense,
which are not things fit to eat,
and even so the verse included them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for אביי's claim about טמא meat.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's ruling that all agree on מלקות for טמא meat before זריקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra word 'והבשר' (ויקרא ז:יט) includes even inedible wood and frankincense.

steps.title: רבא: with impure meat, everyone agrees there are no lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבא agrees the מחלוקת is about a טמא person, but says for טמא meat before זריקה all agree there are no מלקות, because that איסור is linked to the כרת פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They argue about a טמא person. But with טמא meat, everyone agrees he does not get lashes. Why? Since the פסוק 'with his impurity on him, he shall be cut off' does not apply to this meat, the פסוק 'meat that touches anything טמא shall not be eaten' does not apply to it either.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite view from אביי about טמא meat. He says that before זריקה, eating טמא meat brings no מלקות at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא connects the two פסוקים that sit next to each other. The כרת פסוק is about meat after זריקה, so he says the neighboring איסור of טמא meat also only applies after זריקה. So before זריקה there is no איסור of טמא meat to give מלקות for.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
We do not read this פסוק as applying to it
And it will be cut off: the punishment of כרת

steps.confusionAlert: Both אביי and רבא agree the מחלוקת is about a טמא person. They argue only about the case of טמא meat: אביי says all agree there are מלקות, רבא says all agree there are none.

phrases.english: And Rava said: The dispute is about impurity of the body,
but with impurity of the meat,
everyone agrees he is not flogged.
What is the reason?
Since we do not apply to it
'with his impurity on him, and he shall be cut off,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:20. This כרת פסוק is about meat after זריקה.

phrases.english: we also do not apply to it

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהַבָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בְּכׇל טָמֵא לֹא יֵאָכֵל״.
phrases.english: 'And the meat that touches anything impure shall not be eaten.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the opposite position to אביי on the case of טמא meat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For טמא meat eaten before זריקה, all agree there are no מלקות, since the איסור of טמא meat is tied to the כרת פסוק, which applies only after זריקה.

steps.title: Challenge to רבא from wood and frankincense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if 'והבשר' includes even wood and frankincense, how can רבא exclude real meat before זריקה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the Master say: 'And the meat' comes to include wood and frankincense!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא using the same teaching אביי relied on. If the איסור covers wood and frankincense, it should surely cover meat before זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the איסור of טמא meat only applies when the כרת פסוק applies, after זריקה. But wood and frankincense never become 'permitted meat' at all, and still the פסוק includes them. So it seems the איסור is not limited to after זריקה.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't the Master say: an opening that brings a known teaching to challenge someone

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say:
'And the meat' comes to include wood and frankincense!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's position from step 11 using the source from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that eating טמא meat before זריקה brings no מלקות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסוק includes inedible wood and frankincense, which never reach a stage after זריקה, then the איסור is not limited to after זריקה, so meat before זריקה should be included all the more.

steps.title: Wood and frankincense count only once sanctified in a vessel
steps.stepSummary: The wood and frankincense included by 'והבשר' are a case where they were already sanctified in a כלי שרת. That makes them like an offering whose מתירין have all been brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we talking about? Wood and frankincense that were sanctified in a vessel. That makes them like something whose permitting steps have all been done.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 12. Wood and frankincense are only included at the point when they are like meat after זריקה, not before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קשיא assumed that if even wood and frankincense are included, then meat before זריקה should surely be included too. The answer is that wood and frankincense are only included once sanctified in a כלי, which is their version of 'all the מתירין are done.' So רבא can still say meat before זריקה, whose מתירין are not done, is not included.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? A standard way to narrow a case
Became holy by being placed in a כלי שרת (a holy vessel of the Temple)
Permitting factors: the steps that make an offering ready (for example, זריקת הדם)

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
For example, where they were sanctified in a vessel,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the wood and frankincense from the last step.

phrases.english: so it becomes like something whose permitting factors were all offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 in defense of רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the inclusion applies only after sanctification in a vessel.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wood and frankincense are included at any stage, so meat before זריקה should be included even more.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are included only once sanctified in a כלי, which matches meat after זריקה. Meat before זריקה stays excluded.

steps.title: A משנה shows when liability for eating while impure begins
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that an item with מתירין becomes liable once its מתירין are offered. An item without מתירין becomes liable once it is sanctified in a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: anything that has permitting factors is liable from when they are offered. Anything without permitting factors is liable from when it is sanctified in a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to support the answer it just gave. Sanctification in a vessel really is the starting point for things that have no מתירין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sets up two parallel starting points. For meat, it is when the מתירין, like the blood, are offered. For items like frankincense, it is sanctification in a כלי. This confirms that the two moments are equal, just as the answer in step 13 claimed.

keyTerms.meaning: From the time its permitting factors were offered

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
Anything that has permitting factors —
from when its permitting factors were offered.
phrases.notes: The משנה means this is when you become liable for eating it while impure.

phrases.english: Anything that has no permitting factors —
from when it was sanctified in a vessel.

steps.whatToRemember: Meat becomes liable after its מתירין are offered. Wood and frankincense become liable after they are sanctified in a כלי. These two moments are parallel, so רבא still holds: no מלקות for meat before זריקה.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 13 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That sanctification in a כלי is the equivalent of 'all מתירין offered' for items that have no מתירין.

steps.title: Offering a non-kosher animal on the altar: lashes or not?
steps.stepSummary: New topic: someone offers limbs of a בהמה טמאה on the מזבח. ריש לקיש says he gets מלקות; רבי יוחנן says he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if someone offers limbs of a non-kosher animal on the altar, ריש לקיש says he is lashed and רבי יוחנן says he is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion. It quotes a מחלוקת between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a non-kosher animal brought as an offering. The question is whether this act is serious enough to carry מלקות. The reasons for each side come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-kosher animal (here it does not mean ritually impure)
He receives מלקות (lashes)

steps.confusionAlert: In the earlier steps, 'טמא' meant ritually impure (a person or meat with טומאה). Here, 'בהמה טמאה' means a non-kosher kind of animal. It is the same word with a different meaning.

phrases.english: It was stated:
One who offers up the limbs of a non-kosher animal
upon the altar —
Reish Lakish says: he is lashed;
Rabbi Yochanan says: he is not lashed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous discussion was resolved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש: offering a non-kosher animal on the מזבח brings מלקות. רבי יוחנן: it does not.

steps.title: The reasoning: lashes for a prohibition implied by a positive command?
steps.stepSummary: Both agree the Torah implies 'kosher yes, non-kosher no.' They disagree over whether a לאו הבא מכלל עשה carries מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says he is lashed: a kosher animal yes, a non-kosher one no, and you get lashes for a prohibition that comes from a positive command. רבי יוחנן says you do not get lashes for such a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each side of the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah commands bringing kosher animals. That implies a ban on non-kosher ones, but the ban is not stated as a direct 'do not.' ריש לקיש holds that this implied ban, a לאו הבא מכלל עשה, still brings מלקות. רבי יוחנן holds that it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition implied by a positive command, not stated as a direct 'do not'
A kosher animal, yes; a non-kosher animal, no

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole argument rests on one general rule: whether an implied prohibition carries מלקות. That rule matters far beyond the case of offerings.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says he is lashed —
a kosher animal, yes; a non-kosher one, no;

phrases.aramaic: וְלָאו הַבָּא מִכְּלַל עֲשֵׂה לוֹקִין עָלָיו.
phrases.english: and a prohibition that comes from a positive command — one is lashed for it.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר אֵין לוֹקִין עָלָיו –
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says one is not lashed for it —

phrases.aramaic: לָאו הַבָּא מִכְּלַל עֲשֵׂה אֵין לוֹקִין עָלָיו.
phrases.english: a prohibition that comes from a positive command — one is not lashed for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the מחלוקת quoted in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument depends on whether a לאו הבא מכלל עשה brings מלקות. ריש לקיש says yes; רבי יוחנן says no.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: an implied prohibition counts only as a positive command
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes a ברייתא on 'אותה תאכלו' that says an implied prohibition only has the status of an עשה. This goes against ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה objects: 'That you may eat' means not a non-kosher animal, and a prohibition that comes from a positive command counts as a positive command.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה challenges ריש לקיש with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says outright that a לאו הבא מכלל עשה is only an עשה. There are no מלקות for breaking an עשה. So this seems to directly contradict ריש לקיש, who gives מלקות for it.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection (usually from a תנאי source)
'That you may eat': the פסוק about which animals are kosher
A positive command. Breaking it does not bring מלקות

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya raises an objection:
"That you may eat" —
but not a non-kosher animal;
and a prohibition that comes from a positive command is a positive command.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's position as explained in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that a לאו הבא מכלל עשה brings מלקות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls a לאו הבא מכלל עשה only an עשה. An עשה carries no מלקות, so ריש לקיש's ruling seems contradicted.

steps.title: רבי יעקב moves the dispute from non-kosher animals to kosher wild animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב tells רבי ירמיה בר תחליפא that for a בהמה טמאה everyone agrees there is no מלקות. The real dispute is about a חיה: רבי יוחנן says it breaks an עשה, and ריש לקיש says it breaks nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said to רבי ירמיה בר תחליפא: Let me explain it to you. About limbs of a non-kosher animal, everyone agrees. Where they argue is about a wild animal. This is how it was said: רבי יוחנן says he breaks a positive commandment. ריש לקיש says he breaks nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב answers the challenge from step 17 by saying the argument was quoted wrongly. The dispute was never about a non-kosher animal. It was about a kosher wild animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא of 'אותה תאכלו' showed that an implied prohibition is only an עשה, which seemed to go against ריש לקיש. Now everyone agrees that a בהמה טמאה only breaks an עשה, so the problem goes away. The argument shifts to a חיה, and the question there is whether there is even an עשה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: I will explain it to you
A wild (non-domesticated) kosher animal, like a deer
He breaks a positive commandment (no מלקות)
He does not break anything at all

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. בהמה טמאה means a non-kosher animal, and everyone agrees about it. חיה here means a kosher wild animal, and that is where they argue.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov said to
Rabbi Yirmeya bar Tachlifa:
I will explain it to you:
Regarding limbs of a non-kosher animal,
phrases.notes: This is the case from step 15, someone who offers them on the מזבח.

phrases.english: everyone agrees (no one disagrees).
phrases.notes: They agree he only breaks an עשה, so there is no מלקות.

phrases.english: When they disagree, it is about a wild animal;
and this is how it was stated:
Rabbi Yochanan says: He breaks a positive commandment;

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אֵינוֹ עוֹבֵר בִּוְלֹא כְּלוּם.
phrases.english: Reish Lakish says: He does not break anything at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא, אַסְבְּרַהּ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17 by quoting the argument differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-quoting the dispute (והכי איתמר): it moves to a different case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument was about a בהמה טמאה, and ריש לקיש gave מלקות for a לאו הבא מכלל עשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees a בהמה טמאה is only an עשה. The argument is about a חיה: an עשה, or nothing at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: About a חיה: רבי יוחנן says it breaks an עשה, and ריש לקיש says it breaks nothing.

steps.title: The reasoning behind each side about a wild animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק as 'בהמה yes, חיה no', which makes an implied עשה. ריש לקיש says the פסוק only teaches the best way to do the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he breaks a positive commandment, because the Torah means 'a domestic animal, yes; a wild animal, no.' ריש לקיש says he does not break anything, because that פסוק is only about the best way to do the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each אמורא holds his view about bringing a חיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, saying 'bring from בקר וצאן' also means 'not from a חיה'. That is a לאו הבא מכלל עשה, which counts as an עשה. For ריש לקיש, the פסוק only gives the best way (למצוה), so bringing a חיה breaks nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A domestic animal yes; a wild animal no
Only as the best way to do it, not a requirement

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says he breaks a positive commandment:
a domestic animal, yes; a wild animal, no.

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר אֵינוֹ עוֹבֵר עָלָיו בִּוְלֹא כְּלוּם –
phrases.english: Reish Lakish says he does not break anything at all over it:
that is only for the מצוה.
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק of 'בקר וצאן' only shows the best way to do it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר עוֹבֵר בַּעֲשֵׂה – בְּהֵמָה אִין, חַיָּה לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning for the two views quoted in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: 'בקר וצאן' implies 'not a חיה' (an עשה). ריש לקיש: the פסוק is only the best way, so no עשה is broken.

steps.title: רבא challenges ריש לקיש from a ברייתא that excludes wild animals
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא. Without 'בקר וצאן' we would have included a חיה, because the Torah calls deer a 'בהמה'. 'בקר וצאן' teaches: cattle and flock, and not a חיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: If the Torah had only said 'an offering to ה׳, from animals,' I would have said wild animals are included in 'animal.' That is how the Torah uses the word: 'These are the animals you may eat: ox, sheep, goat, deer, gazelle...' So the Torah says 'cattle and flock': I told you cattle and flock, and not a wild animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a ברייתא to attack ריש לקיש's view that bringing a חיה breaks nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בהמה alone could include a חיה, as the פסוק about kosher animals shows. The extra words 'בקר וצאן' are there to leave out the חיה. That sounds like a real exclusion, not just advice about the best way, which goes against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection (from a source)
A wild animal is included in the word 'animal'
Cattle and flock (sheep and goats)
Therefore the פסוק says

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
Had it said 'an offering to ה׳, from animals,'
I would have said: a wild animal is included in 'animal,'
like what is stated:
'These are the animals that you may eat:
the ox, the sheep, and the goat,
the deer and the gazelle, etc.'
phrases.notes: Deer and gazelle are wild animals, yet this פסוק calls them 'בהמה'.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: 'cattle and flock':

phrases.aramaic: בָּקָר וָצֹאן אָמַרְתִּי לְךָ, וְלֹא חַיָּה.
phrases.english: I told you cattle and flock, and not a wild animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's view from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש, who says bringing a חיה breaks nothing and that 'בקר וצאן' is only the best way.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats 'בקר וצאן' as deliberately leaving out a חיה, which suggests a real exclusion and not just advice.

steps.title: The ברייתא considers whether a wild animal is valid if already brought
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: maybe one should not bring a חיה, but if he did, it counts? It compares this to a student told to bring wheat who brings wheat and barley. He added to his teacher's words without going against them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe he should not bring one, but if he did, it is valid? What is this like? Like a student whose teacher told him, 'Bring me wheat,' and he brought wheat and barley. He did not go against his teacher's words. He only added to them, so it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and raises a possible idea: maybe a חיה is valid after the fact. It is setting up this idea so that it can respond to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wheat-and-barley parable shows why someone might think bringing a חיה is only adding to the command, not breaking it. This idea sounds like ריש לקיש's approach. The ברייתא brings it up as a possibility it is preparing to answer.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought
Don't bring it at the start, but if he did, it counts
What is this comparable to?
Going against his words
Adding to his words

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the ברייתא's final ruling. The word יכול signals a possibility the ברייתא is about to respond to.

phrases.english: One might think he should not bring it,
but if he did bring it, it is valid?
For what is this comparable to?
To a student whose teacher said to him
'Bring me wheat,'
and he brought him wheat and barley,
that he is not like one who goes against his words,
but rather adds to his words, and it is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יָבִיא, וְאִם הֵבִיא כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא רבא quoted, raising a possible idea that a חיה is valid after the fact.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a חיה brought as a קרבן is valid after the fact, even though one should not bring it at the start.

steps.title: The Torah repeats 'cattle and flock' to exclude a wild animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers its own question. The Torah says 'בקר וצאן' again, meaning: I told you cattle and flock, and not a חיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'cattle and flock.' This means: I told you to bring cattle and flock, and not a wild animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from step 21. It points to a second mention of 'בקר וצאן' in the פסוק and reads it as God saying: cattle and flock, and not a חיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first mention of 'בקר וצאן' already taught that a חיה should not be brought. The question was whether a חיה still counts if someone brought it anyway. The second mention adds that God is actively ruling out the חיה, so bringing one is not just a lesser way of doing the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches. This phrase introduces the פסוק that answers a question.
Cattle.
Flock (sheep and goats).
I told you. The Torah is read as God speaking directly.

phrases.english: The verse says: "cattle and flock"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:3 and 1:10. This is the Torah mentioning cattle and flock a second time.

phrases.english: I told you cattle and flock,
and not a wild animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The repeated 'בקר וצאן' shows that God excludes a חיה. So a חיה does not count even after the fact.

steps.title: The student told to bring only wheat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא retells the student parable. The teacher said 'bring me only wheat,' so bringing barley too is disobeying him, not adding to his words.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this like? It is like a student whose teacher told him, 'Bring me nothing but wheat,' and he brought wheat and barley. He is not like someone adding to his teacher's words. He is like someone going against them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a parable to explain its answer. It flips the parable from step 21: once the teacher says 'only wheat,' the barley breaks his instruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21 the teacher just said 'bring wheat,' so extra barley looked like a harmless addition. Here the teacher said 'only wheat,' just as the repeated פסוק says 'only cattle and flock.' That turns the extra item into disobedience, which supports the view that a חיה breaks a command and does not just miss the best way of doing the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this like? This phrase introduces a parable.
Only, nothing but. Here it is the key word in the teacher's instruction.
Adding to his words: doing more than told, without going against the instruction.
Going against his words: disobeying the instruction.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the parable in step 21. There the teacher said 'bring wheat,' so barley was only an extra. Here he said 'ONLY wheat,' so barley is disobedience. The word 'only' changes everything.
steps.whyThisMatters: This parable turns the ברייתא into a challenge to ריש לקיש. He said the פסוק only teaches the best way to do the מצוה, but the ברייתא treats a חיה as going against the Torah's command.

phrases.english: To what is this similar?
To a student whose teacher told him
"Bring me nothing but wheat,"
and he brought him wheat and barley,
he is not like one adding to his words
but like one going against his words,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the answer from step 22 with a parable that reverses the parable from step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the Torah said 'only cattle and flock,' bringing a חיה is disobeying God's command and not just adding to it.
